title: Axiomatic stable homotopy 10 — What is the endomorphism ring of the identity functor on the stable homotopy category?
statement: What is the endomorphism ring of the identity functor on the stable homotopy category? The ring Z splits off this ring, including by multiples of the identity, and projecting off by observing what the natural transformation does to the identity map of S^0. If we assume the generating hypothesis, any element of the kernel is a natural self-phantom map of X for all X. This must force it to be 0, but why? And do we really need the generating hypothesis?

title: Erdős Problem #413 — Let $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct primes dividing $n$. Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $m<n$, we have $m+\omega(m) \leq n$?
statement:
Let $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct primes dividing $n$. Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $m<n$, we have $m+\omega(m) \leq n$?

title: Turán’s tetrahedron-density conjecture
statement:
Let $\operatorname{ex}_3(n,F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no subhypergraph isomorphic to $F$, and let $K_4^{(3)}$ be the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on four vertices. Define
\[
\pi(F):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{ex}_3(n,F)}{\binom{n}{3}}.
\]
The conjecture is
\[
\pi\bigl(K_4^{(3)}\bigr)=\frac{5}{9}.
\]

title: Question 3: Boundary-to-center distance for analytic vector-valued functions
statement:
Let $D$ be the closed unit disk, let $N$ be a (usually very big) positive integer, and let $\|\cdot\|_p$ denote the $\ell^p$ norm on $\mathbb{C}^N$. Let $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_k$ be $k$ functions in $H^\infty(D,\mathbb{C}^N)$. For each fixed $z\in D$, define
$$
M(z)=\operatorname{span}\{f_1(z),f_2(z),\ldots,f_k(z)\}.
$$
Suppose that $g\in H^\infty(D,\mathbb{C}^N)$ satisfies $\|g(z)\|_p\le 1$ for all $z\in D$ and
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{\ell^p}(g(z),M(z))\le\varepsilon
$$
for almost every $z\in T$. Does it follow that
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{\ell^p}(g(0),M(0))\le\varepsilon?
$$
The report states that the answer is no, by an almost embarrassingly simple counterexample.
